**Triage: lands in `scripts/check-side-effects-array.mjs`; `domain:devx`; `priority:p2` — the gate is blind in exactly the failure class it exists to prevent.**

`evaluatePackage` walks ONE graph (`walkEntryGraph(sourceBarrelAbs)`, the single `src/index.*` that `deriveSpellingMap` finds), while `manifestEntryForms` collects **every** entry form the manifest publishes — each one a module a consumer's bundler can resolve to. ⇒ a package with more than one entry has its `sideEffects` array compared against an enumeration derived from **one** of them.

A registrar that loads at import time and is reachable only from a secondary entry is therefore invisible: never proposed as MISSING, and if the array *does* name it, it reads as STALE — so the gate actively pushes toward removing a correct entry.

⭐ That last consequence is why this is p2 rather than a coverage nit: the gate does not merely miss the defect, it can **argue for introducing one**.

⇒ In scope: walk every published entry form, not just the source barrel. ⚠️ Establish the multi-entry population first — if it is currently empty the fix is still right but the priority claim rests on future packages rather than present ones, and that should be said plainly in the PR rather than left implied.

⛔ Do not make the array authoritative over the walk to resolve a disagreement; the walk is the check.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

## ⭐ The population triage told you to establish first — established, and it changes the PR's argument

Triage wrote: ⚠️ 「Establish the multi-entry population first — if it is currently empty the fix is still right but the priority claim rests on **future** packages rather than present ones, and that should be said plainly in the PR rather than left implied.」

Measured on `origin/main` = `3984bab5a` (tip committed 2026-09-10T23:09:04Z), by re-deriving `manifestEntryForms`' own rule over every workspace manifest — **46 scanned**, and it is a **re-derivation**, ⛔ not the gate's own reader, so re-run it inside the worktree before relying on it:

| package declaring an ARRAY | forms `manifestEntryForms` returns | what the second form actually is |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `@object-ui/app-shell` | `dist/index.js` · `src/styles.css` | ⚠️ a **CSS asset** — ⛔ not a module a graph walk can traverse |
| `@object-ui/layout` | `dist/index.js` · `dist/index.umd.cjs` | ⚠️ the `import`/`require` pair of the **same** entry `.` — a second **format**, ⛔ not a second entry point |

⇒ **two** array-declaring packages, both 「multi-entry」 by the function's own count, and ⛔ **neither has a second entry point with its own source module**. The genuine population is **zero today**.

⭐ That is not a reason to drop the card — it is the sentence the PR has to carry, and it also **redirects the fix**: the two forms that exist are exactly the two shapes an inverse-of-`toPublished` cannot map to a source file. ⇒ 「fail loudly when it cannot」 would fire on both of today's packages on day one.

## ⛔ One number in the card is wrong — ⛔ do not carry it forward

The card says 「`@object-ui/app-shell` publishes **31** entries」. **31 is the length of its `sideEffects` array**; its manifest publishes **2** forms, one of which is the stylesheet. ⇒ the card's cost concern (「a walk per entry has to stay a single de-duplicated module set or the walk time multiplies」) rests on a misread figure and, as written, has no present instance behind it.

⚠️ ⭐ The card is otherwise sound and its **defect** is real — this correction is to one premise, ⛔ not to the finding. And note what it is an instance of: a count in prose that no instrument re-derives, which objectui#7833 was carded for a day earlier.

## ⭐ `@object-ui/types` is the card's proof and is ⛔ NOT in the population

It publishes **12** export entries including `./zod`, and its `./zod` barrel is genuinely unreachable from `src/index.ts` — the card measured that and it is the real demonstration. But it declares `sideEffects: false`, and `readArrayPackages` takes **array** declarations only. ⇒ it proves the defect and ⛔ cannot be the fixture that pins it.
